subject: physics
question_text: Why are shock absorbers used in motor cycles and cars?

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), Unit 5 SHORT ANSWER. The mark split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed for this question, so appearances[] stays empty.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The jerk
lines: On an uneven road the vehicle receives
a jerk — a sudden change of momentum.
steps.margin_note: Open with impulse. Without it there is no way to talk about the time at all.
steps.why: A bump is not a force question, it is an impulse question: the road hands the vehicle a fixed change of momentum.
common_mistakes: Answering only "to give comfort", with no physics.

recall.must_convey: That the bump gives a jerk, which is a change of momentum, and impulse = F × Δt.
accept: jerk is a change of momentum

steps.memory_tip: Think impulse, not force: the bump fixes the momentum change Δp.

steps.label: What is fixed
lines: The bump decides Δp, so that change
cannot be avoided. Only the TIME taken
for the change can be altered.
steps.margin_note: This is the hinge of the answer — say plainly which quantity you cannot change.
steps.why: You cannot argue the momentum change away. Every design choice left is about how long the change is spread over.
common_mistakes: Claiming shock absorbers reduce the change in momentum. They do not — they stretch its duration.

recall.must_convey: That the change in momentum is fixed by the bump and only the time can be changed.
accept: only the time can be increased
delta p is fixed only delta t changes
momentum change fix, time matrame marchagalam
reject: jerk is a change of momentum

steps.memory_tip: Δp cannot be changed — the only free quantity is the TIME it is spread over.

steps.label: The relation
lines: for a fixed change of momentum.
steps.margin_note: Write the inverse proportion. It is the sentence "longer time, smaller force" in symbols.
steps.why: Once Δp is fixed, force and time trade off exactly. Doubling the time halves the force.
common_mistakes: Writing F ∝ Δt, which says the opposite of the answer.

recall.must_convey: That force is inversely proportional to the time, for a fixed change of momentum.
accept: force is inversely proportional to time
F equals delta p by delta t

steps.memory_tip: F = Δp/Δt: same Δp, double the time, half the force.

steps.label: The conclusion
lines: A shock absorber spreads the jerk over
so the vehicle and the rider are safer.
steps.margin_note: End on the vehicle and the rider. That is what the question actually asked about.
steps.why: The spring and oil let the wheel move up slowly instead of the whole vehicle jolting, which is the longer Δt in physical form.
common_mistakes: Stopping at the formula without saying what it does for the rider.

recall.must_convey: That the shock absorber lengthens the time, so the force on the vehicle and rider is smaller.
accept: increases the time so force is less
reject: force is inversely proportional to time

steps.memory_tip: The spring lengthens Δt, so the force on the rider drops. End the answer on that sentence.

insider_note: Four marks in one sequence — impulse, Δp is fixed, F ∝ 1/Δt, then the rider. An answer that says only "for comfort" loses three of them.
